rv.q: Theo's production is pitched well between the silly and the sardonic, and in the small space of what is now the Fred Anzevino Theatre ( named in honor of Theo's late founder and artistic director ), it also feels connected to its creators' long-ago Chicago fringe roots.

Danny Kapinos’ playful and powerful production will make audiences laugh at the preposterous plot while pondering how this futuristic fantasy potently portrays the politics and ecological concerns of today.
All elements in the show own this attitude throughout.
Theo’s production is chock full of tongue in cheek humor and crystal clear vocals as the cast uses every corner of the stage.

Urinetown the Musical, consistently reminds the audience that great humor can also bring uncomfortable truths to light, and at Theo, it’s likely you’ll delve deeper as you watch and thoroughly enjoy the production.

cn.t: Critics praise Theo Ubique's energetic, immersive production of the satirical musical, highlighting sharp humor, strong vocals, and inventive cabaret-style staging that engages audiences in the dystopian comedy.
